situation: Touch files under ~ or /Volumes (outside the Cowork sandbox)
note: Built-in Read/Write/Edit only reach connected folders. filesystem-enhanced reaches the whole Mac. For CHANGING code that already exists, use safe-edit (next entry) -- write_file rewrites the whole file.

situation: Changing code or text in a file that already exists — one file, or the same change across many
note: safe_edit replaces the matched text only -- it cannot add or drop anything outside the edit radius, and it refuses an ambiguous match instead of guessing. safe_edit_many does the same change across a list of files ALL-OR-NOTHING: nothing is written until every file has been planned and passed its structural gate, and a file with no match is reported as SKIPPED by name, never silently. This replaced smalledit (retired 2026-08-22). Use safe_preview first when unsure. filesystem-enhanced write_file rewrites the WHOLE file -- do not use it to change existing code.

situation: Run a command on Mikey's real Mac, his LAN, or pop over ssh
note: The sandbox bash has no LAN route. system_exec runs as bard on the Mac; ssh user@192.168.x.x for pop. Use git CLI through it for all git work.

situation: Session start, remembering, or recalling anything from past sessions
note: brain_init at session start. Write memories DURING work, not at the end. After tasks: brain_reflect.

situation: Launching or monitoring a training / distillation / fine-tuning run
note: Read protocol training-run-management first. tmux pane for visibility, native W&B, step-stamped checkpoints, verify liftoff after 30s.

situation: Current-world facts, papers, citations, anything post-cutoff
note: Search before claiming. For HF models/datasets/papers there are also hf paper_search / hub_repo_search tools.

situation: MCP server or tool failures, errors, broken tools
note: Run ~/Code/harness/check-contracts.sh — it probes every wired server's tools/list, diffs against tool-contract.json, checks handlers against their schemas and validates documented claims. Logs at ~/Library/Logs/Claude/. Protocol: tool-auto-repair. (tools-registry was unwired 2026-08-19; the contract checks replace and exceed registry_summary.)

situation: What time is it / elapsed time / any time-of-day assumption
note: Never guess the time; response timestamps come from this.

situation: Locating a project or code on the Mac
note: Check the filesystem before claiming something does or does not exist.

situation: Context running long / handoff to a future session
note: Write the continuation note BEFORE context is lost. Protocol: auto-continuation.

situation: Verifying claims, math, or suspicious confident reasoning
note: Compute, don't assert. Run numbers through code; skills: pattern-match-check.

situation: Bulk reading, summarising, or fetching material that is NOT already in context
note: A 35B model sits idle on pop. Measured 2026-08-21: ~2.7x faster than doing it in context, and 6.1x less context spent, because the raw pages never enter it. Every job must carry a check -- the server refuses work it cannot verify, deliberately. search_and_summarize is the ONLY search tool here and is rate-limited, one at a time. DO IT YOURSELF instead when the text is already in context, when the job needs interpretation rather than transcription, or when being right matters more than being checkable: ornith transcribes faithfully, it does not interpret.

situation: A task may be too big to do in one pass — ask whether it should be broken up first
note: Mikey's rule, given 2026-08-21: ASK whether the task should be broken up. If yes, call decomposer. The asking is the step -- do not skip it and do not silently decide either way. decompose() splits a prompt into sub-tasks; classify() judges the shape of the problem first; rlm_execute() runs the recursive form, treating the input as an external environment rather than as context to be read whole. Backed by Ollama at localhost:11434 -- endpoint verified HTTP 200 on 2026-08-19 and again 2026-08-21. DO IT YOURSELF instead when the task is already one step, when breaking it up would cost more than doing it, or when the pieces would need each other's results to be written -- that is a plan, not a decomposition. The failure mode of routing this tool is OVER-decomposition: turning a two-minute job into six coordinated ones.
